name: SCHISTOSOMAL - IgM
interpretation:
This test is useful for detection of antibodies to Schistosoma species.
Negative: the absence of antibodies to Schistosoma suggests that the patient has not been exposed to the trematode. A single negative
result should not be used to rule-out infection with Schistosoma species.

Cut off  10 DU  
Positive >11
DU		 Antibodies against the pathogen are present.
There has been a contact with the antigen (pathogen resp. vaccine).
Equivocal  9 – 11
DU		 Antibodies against the pathogen could not be detected clearly. It is recommended to repeat the test with a fresh sample in 2 to 4 weeks. If the result is equivocal again the sample is jadjed as negative.
Negative <9 DU The sample contains no antibodies against the pathogen.A previous contact with the antigen (pathogen resp. vaccine) is unlikely.
Diagnosis of an infectious disease should not be established on the basis of a single test result. A precise diagnosis should take into consideration clinical history, symptomatology as well as serological data. In immunocompomised patient and newborns serological data only have restricted value.

Equivocal: consider repeat testing on a new serum sample in 1 to 2 weeks.
Positive: results suggest infection with Schistosoma. False-positive results may occur in setting of infection with other helminthes, including
with Echinococcus or Taenia species results should be considered alongside other clinical findings and exposure history.
Limitation:
1. Sensitivity for detection of antibodies to each of Schistosoma species cannot be evaluated for this assay.
2. Some patients may remain seropositive by this assay following treatment an clearance of infection.
3. Positive results should be confirmed with other laboratory finding [e.g. ova and parent examination) clinical symptom and sutable
exposure history.
